Free trade is absolutely a good thing. It has pulled more people out of poverty, improved education levels, improved standards of living, and similar markers for a better life than anything else in the history of the world.

Free trade also benefits both sides due to comparative advantage. The TLDR of which is that Japan is vastly better at e.g. fishing than Russia, while Russia is vastly better at producing oil, so both sides benefit more from the exchange than they would trying to fish out of icebound Russian ports or drilling for oil in Tokyo.

The downside to free trade is that its losers are highly visible (muy entire faktory got shipped overseas!), while the net benefit is less visible (if every manufactured good you buy became 10% cheaper over a span of five years, would you even notice?). This leads to political squabbling.

The overwhelming majority of economists say that free trade is very positive, and for good reason. You mentioned 'the billions who starve,' but the truth is that poverty around the world has been sharply reduced in recent decades. 'Globalism' is to thank for this. The next time you go shopping, ask yourself if you'd rather pay more money just to ensure all of your purchases were made here; that's what you get from protectionism.

In my opinion you can have a free trade with countries that have laws and labor rates similar to ours. I don't see much issue there. I see a huge issue with countries where people make $1 an hr and labor or environmental laws are almost non existent.
